newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila offers Nauru fertiliser firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Manila offers Nauru fertiliser firm stake.

text.p: The Philippines had offered to sell its stake in a joint venture fertiliser company to its partner in the venture, the Pacific island nation of Nauru.

Visiting Nauru President Lagumot Harris agreed to consider the proposal of Philippine President Fidel Ramos that Manila sell its stake in the Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corp (Philphos) to other parties if the Pacific island nation does not want to buy out the firm, Friday's presidential palace statement said.
Philphos is 50 percent owned by the National Development Co, the equity investment arm of the Philippine government, and 50 percent by the Nauru government.
The country's largest fertiliser company is posting net losses due to yen-denominated debt incurred in the construction of its plant in central Philippines in the early 1980s.
Philphos officials said the firm accumulated 5.2 billion pesos in debt in the 1980s.
The firm's debts ballooned to 32 billion pesos as of November 1995 due to peso devaluation and yen appreciation against the U.S. dollar, Philphos said.
